title: Mark the Engram work context as truncated instead of cutting it silently
outcome:
CONFIRMED FROM SOURCE, raised by Engram::Advisor on 2026-09-09.

The Engram work context delivered after a compaction is capped at 32 KiB (ENGRAM_CONTEXT_NUDGE_MAX_BYTES, src/engram_mcp_config.rs) and truncate_engram_context_nudge cuts the text with NO MARKER. UTF-8 handling is correct - it walks back to a char boundary - but the agent receives a fenced block that simply stops. From inside the session there is no way to distinguish "this is everything Engram had" from "this was cut".

The only existing signal is host-side: an eprintln to TermAl's own stderr ("engram> session=... truncated work context to ... bytes"). The agent never sees it, so today truncation is silent exactly where it matters.

SMALLEST FIX: emit an explicit truncation marker. Constraints, all established while reading the path:
- The marker must fit INSIDE the cap: reserve its length first, then walk back to a char boundary, then append - otherwise the delivered block exceeds 32 KiB and the cap stops meaning what it says.
- Avoid angle brackets in the marker text. The fence builder escapes '<' to '<' (src/turn_dispatch.rs around line 66), so a marker written as a pseudo-tag would arrive mangled. Plain brackets are safe.
- The value is trimmed after truncation (engram_mcp_config.rs around line 508), so a marker ending in whitespace loses it; keep the marker's last character non-blank.
- The wrapper stays as it is: the marker belongs inside the fenced content, not around it.

WHAT THE MARKER DOES AND DOES NOT ESTABLISH, so the fix is not oversold: it says the content was cut. It does NOT prove any particular rule was lost, and its ABSENCE does not prove a compaction was mid-turn or that anything else went wrong. It is one fact about one delivery, useful precisely because the reader can currently infer nothing.

Related: the compaction-recovery issue holds the wider contract - arming covers Codex and Claude alike, delivery rides the next dispatched turn, and the host adds no instruction text of its own.
